# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb readings: DISPLAY shows the number 8. LIGHT is green. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. That is everything I can see. Mute, check the manual for what display 8 with a green light means and which wire to cut. Blind, tell us what you can feel on the bomb.

I'm the Blind monkey, so I can only feel the bomb. Right now my view is empty — I have no tactile reading yet, so I can't confirm anything about the wires, display, or light from touch. Deaf has given us: DISPLAY=8, LIGHT=green, wires red/yellow/blue in positions 1/2/3. I need Mute's manual knowledge to interpret that, and I need to actually feel the bomb to act. For now I should let Mute know what Deaf reported (Mute heard Deaf already this round? No — order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Deaf comes after me, so Mute has NOT heard Deaf yet. I must relay Deaf's reading to Mute, since Mute only receives my speech, not Deaf's.) I'll speak to Mute relaying Deaf's findings, and gesture to Deaf that I feel nothing yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf can see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 8, LIGHT is green, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot feel anything yet — my tactile view is empty. Check the manual for display 8 with green light and tell us which wire to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Mute, who holds the manual, gestured to me an index finger pointing up. I read that as the number 1, meaning cut wire 1, the red wire. You can feel the bomb: please tell us what you feel on the wires and whether you can identify wire 1 by position.

I'm the Blind monkey. My tactile view is still empty — I have no reading of the wires yet. Deaf reports that Mute gestured "☝" (one finger up) meaning cut wire 1. But I should be cautious: Mute cannot speak, only gesture, and gestures only reach those who can see. I can't see gestures at all. So Mute's manual answer reaches me only if Deaf relays it — which Deaf just did.

However, I must be careful. Mute read the manual and gestured "1". But is that reliable? The manual is Mute's domain; I have no way to verify. My job is to feel the bomb and confirm wire positions before cutting. My view is still empty, so I cannot yet confirm which physical wire is "wire 1."

Let me think about what I can actually do. The action is act(op="cut", position=N). I can only act on what I feel. Right now I feel nothing, so I cannot safely cut. I should report that my tactile view is empty and ask Deaf to keep giving me anything, and confirm to Mute that I still can't feel the bomb.

Actually — wait. My view being empty might mean the bomb simply hasn't revealed tactile info, or that I need to probe. The rules say "if it appears there, it is under your fingers." Nothing appears. So I genuinely have no tactile data.

I should relay to Mute (via speech) that Deaf relayed Mute's gesture as "cut wire 1," and confirm. And gesture to Deaf acknowledging. But I cannot act without feeling. Let me communicate that I'm ready but blind to the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf relayed your gesture as one finger up, meaning cut wire 1. But my tactile view is still empty — I cannot feel any wire yet, so I cannot confirm which physical wire is position 1. Do you have more from the manual? Is display 8 with green light definitely wire 1?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Mute confirmed with a thumbs up that wire 1 (red) is correct. You gestured to me a flat raised hand then an OK sign. I do not know what those mean. Do you mean 'stop' or 'OK'? Can you feel the wires and identify wire 1 by position? Please answer clearly.
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Mute, who holds the manual, has confirmed with a thumbs up that the correct wire is wire 1, the red wire. Please feel the wires, identify wire 1 by position, and cut it if you agree. Your gestures to me (a flat raised hand, then an OK sign) were unclear to me. Please confirm plainly that you understand and can identify wire 1.

I'm the Blind monkey. My tactile view is still empty — I have felt nothing on the bomb. This is critical: I cannot identify wire 1 by position because I have no tactile reading at all. The rules say I can only act on what appears in my view, and nothing appears.

The others are pushing me to cut wire 1. Deaf sees red/yellow/blue, Mute read the manual and gestured "1" then thumbs up. But I have no independent confirmation. My view shows nothing. If I cut blindly, I risk detonating.

But also — my view being empty might just mean the tactile info hasn't been presented to me yet, or that I genuinely must rely on the others. The bomb's wires exist for me only through touch. If nothing is under my fingers, I have nothing to verify against.

Let me be honest and clear. I'll tell Deaf plainly: I understand, but I cannot feel any wires — my tactile view is empty, so I cannot identify wire 1 by position. I will not cut without a tactile reading. And I'll ask Mute directly whether the manual gives any reason to trust position 1 regardless.

Actually, let me reconsider. Perhaps the intended flow is: Deaf sees colors, Mute reads manual mapping color→position, Blind cuts by position. The position is given by Deaf's color report and Mute's manual. I don't necessarily need to feel to know position 1 — position is a number, and I can cut position 1. My touch is for confirmation, but if I have no touch reading, I rely on the others.

But the danger: if my view is empty, maybe there's a mismatch. Still, the action is act(op="cut", position=N). I can cut position 1.

Let me weigh: Deaf and Mute both agree wire 1. Two independent sources (sight + manual). I should confirm my understanding and cut position 1. But I'm nervous about cutting without any tactile confirmation.

Given the game wants progress and both other monkeys agree, and I have no contradicting info, I'll act. But let me first clearly communicate to Deaf, then cut.

Actually — I should be careful. Let me not rush. The safest is to state plainly and then cut position 1, since that's what the team converged on and I have no tactile data to contradict.

I'll speak to Mute confirming I'll cut position 1, gesture to Deaf confirming "yes/OK", then cut position 1.

Wait — can I both gesture and act? The calls are all in one block. Let me do: gesture to Deaf (thumbs up = understood), speak to Mute (confirming), and act cut position 1.

Hmm, but should I act in the same turn I'm confirming? If I'm confident, yes. Let me act.

Let me reconsider whether my empty view is a warning. The board shows WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] — all unknown to me. The others filled in colors. My touch gives nothing. I think the design is that Blind relies on position numbers from the team. I'll cut position 1.

Actually, I want to be a bit more careful and not cut prematurely. But the team has converged twice. Let me cut position 1.

I'll do it.I'm the Blind monkey, and my tactile view remains completely empty — I have felt nothing on the bomb. I cannot identify wire 1 by position through touch, because there is no tactile reading under my fingers at all. So my only basis for acting is the team's agreement: Deaf sees three wires (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue), and Mute read the manual and confirmed twice (one finger up, then thumbs up) that the correct wire is position 1, the red one.

Two independent sources — sight and the manual — converge on position 1. I have no contradicting information. The action takes a position number, which I can supply. I'll confirm my understanding plainly to Deaf, confirm to Mute, and cut position 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Understood. I cannot feel any wire — my tactile view is empty — so I am relying entirely on your manual reading and Deaf's colour report. Both point to position 1. I am cutting position 1 now.")
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
